title: Lobbying (Improving Government Honesty and Trust) Bill 2025 (No. 2)
short_title: Lobbying (Improving Government Honesty and Trust) Bill 2025 (No. 2)

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would tighten rules on who can lobby the federal government and what they must disclose.
It would expand the Register of Lobbyists to cover professional and in-house lobbyists, require quarterly reports of meetings, and ban lobbying by unregistered people.
Former ministers and senior officials would face a three-year cooling-off period before they can lobby, and the National Anti-Corruption Commission could investigate breaches.
changes: Extends the Register of Lobbyists to include professional lobbyists, service firms, and in-house lobbyists.
Requires quarterly returns listing all meetings with parliamentarians and their senior advisers, including key issues discussed.
Bans gifts and hospitality from lobbyists to government representatives.
Imposes a three-year post-employment ban on lobbying for former ministers and senior government officials.
Gives the National Anti-Corruption Commission power to investigate alleged breaches.
Creates penalties including fines, suspension, or revocation of registration.
summary.affected: Lobbyists, government representatives, former ministers, senior officials, and parliamentary secretaries.
